newsitem.title: USA: Tucson Electric to sell $132 mln bonds.
newsitem.headline: Tucson Electric to sell $132 mln bonds.

text.p: Tucson Electric Power Co Wednesday received approval from the Arizona Corporation Commission to issue $131.8 million of tax exempt pollution control revenue bonds.

The bonds will finance $20 million of new pollution control facilities at the Navajo Generating Station in Coconino County, Ariz., and will refinance $31.4 million of previously issued bonds which financed pollution control facilities at the Navajo Station and $80.4 million of previously issued bonds which financed facilities at the San Juan Generating Station near Farmington, N.M.
The new financings, which are expected to be at fixed rates and unsecured, will lower the company's net cost of funds by extending the bonds' maturities and avoiding sinking fund payments.
The new bond issuance is expected to be completed by the end of April, the company said.

The outstanding bonds, which will be refinanced, will be called following completion of the sale. They are a $47.9 million 6.25 percent issue due 2003; a $32.5 million 6.10 percent issue due 2007; a $16.7 million variable rate issue due 2031; and a $14.7 million variable rate issue also due 2031.
The new series of bonds have been rated as senior unsecured debt by Moody's Investors Service at B2, Fitch Investors Service at B+ and Standard & Poor's Corp. at B-.
